author: NorthEast News Desk
body: CVC Capital Partners has entered final negotiations to buy the mainland China operations of contact-lens maker Ginko International from EQT, four people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

The potential transaction could value the business at $700 million to $800 million including debt. EQT had sought at least $1 billion, and the financial terms have not been finalized. The talks could still end without an agreement.

Ginko was founded in Taiwan and makes conventional and disposable contact lenses along with lens-care products. Mainland China is its largest sales market. The investment was made in 2022 by Baring Private Equity Asia, which later combined with EQT.

EQT previously agreed to sell the business to Advent International, but that deal fell through. EQT and JPMorgan declined to comment on the latest talks, while CVC and Goldman Sachs did not respond to Reuters. A completed sale would give investors another measure of private-equity appetite for Chinese consumer-health assets.
dek: Sources say a possible deal for the contact-lens maker’s mainland operations could value the business at $700 million to $800 million including debt.
headline: CVC enters final talks for EQT’s Ginko China business
